Photo-card description for the speaking exam

cards.front: When do you use the preterite rather than the imperfect in Spanish?
cards.back: The preterite describes completed single actions in the past; the imperfect describes ongoing, repeated or background situations.

cards.front: Give the first person preterite of celebrar.
cards.back: Celebré - I celebrated. Note the written accent on the final e; without it, celebre is the subjunctive.

cards.front: How do you say in my opinion in Spanish, at higher level?
cards.back: En mi opinión, or a mi parecer, or desde mi punto de vista.

cards.front: How do you form the superlative in Spanish?
cards.back: Definite article plus más or menos plus adjective, e.g. la fiesta más importante.

cards.front: Give three linking words that raise your writing grade.
cards.back: Sin embargo (however), aunque (although), por lo tanto (therefore), ya que (since).

cloze: The Spanish {{c1::preterite}} tense describes completed actions in the past.
The Spanish {{c1::imperfect}} tense describes what used to happen or was happening.

topics.name: Theme 4 Future Aspirations, Study and Work

cards.front: How do you form the near future tense in Spanish?
cards.back: Ir conjugated plus a plus the infinitive, e.g. voy a estudiar - I am going to study.

cards.front: How do you form the simple future of regular verbs?
cards.back: Add é, ás, á, emos, éis, án to the infinitive, e.g. estudiaré - I will study.

cards.front: How do you form the conditional?
cards.back: Add ía, ías, ía, íamos, íais, ían to the infinitive, e.g. me gustaría - I would like.

cards.front: Which mood follows cuando when talking about the future?
cards.back: The present subjunctive, e.g. cuando termine mis estudios - when I finish my studies.

cards.front: Translate: I would like to work abroad because I want to improve my Spanish.
cards.back: Me gustaría trabajar en el extranjero porque quiero mejorar mi español.

cloze: The near future is formed with {{c1::ir}} plus {{c2::a}} plus the infinitive.
Me gustaría means {{c1::I would like}} and uses the {{c2::conditional}} tense.
After cuando referring to the future, Spanish uses the {{c1::subjunctive}}.

topics.name: Theme 5 International and Global Dimension
subtopics: Environmental problems and solutions

Translation into and out of Spanish

cards.front: How do you say we should recycle more in Spanish?
cards.back: Deberíamos reciclar más.

cards.front: What does hay que plus infinitive express?
cards.back: An impersonal obligation - one must, it is necessary to.

cards.front: Give three environmental problems in Spanish.
cards.back: La contaminación (pollution), el calentamiento global (global warming), la deforestación (deforestation), la sequía (drought).

cards.front: What is the impersonal se used for?
cards.back: To say something is done in general without naming who does it, e.g. se recicla el plástico - plastic is recycled.

cards.front: How many words should a higher-tier extended writing answer be?
cards.back: Around 130 to 150 words, using at least two tenses and developed opinions.

cloze: {{c1::Hay que}} plus an infinitive expresses an impersonal obligation.
La {{c1::contaminación}} means pollution and el {{c2::calentamiento global}} means global warming.
The higher-tier extended writing task requires about {{c1::130 to 150}} words.

cards.front: Explain the difference between ser and estar.
cards.back: Ser is for permanent or defining characteristics, origin, profession and time. Estar is for temporary states, moods and location.

cards.front: When do you use por and when para?
cards.back: Por for cause, exchange, duration and movement through. Para for purpose, destination, deadline and recipient.

cards.front: Where do object pronouns usually go in Spanish?
cards.back: Before the conjugated verb, or attached to the end of an infinitive, gerund or positive command.

cards.front: Name three tenses that will lift a higher-tier written answer.
cards.back: The preterite, the conditional and the subjunctive, alongside the present and near future.

cards.front: Give a fast listening exam strategy.
cards.back: Read the questions before the recording, predict likely vocabulary, and listen actively for numbers, negatives and time markers on the first play.

cards.front: Which five words change meaning only because of a written accent?
cards.back: sí (yes) versus si (if), él (he) versus el (the), tú (you) versus tu (your), más (more) versus mas (but), sólo/solo and qué (what, in questions) versus que (that).

cloze: {{c1::Ser}} is used for permanent characteristics and {{c2::estar}} for temporary states and location.
{{c1::Por}} expresses cause or duration, while {{c2::para}} expresses purpose or destination.
Object pronouns go {{c1::before}} the conjugated verb in Spanish.
The word {{c1::sí}} with an accent means yes, while si without an accent means if.
